cuisine: Sanuki udon house standing inside the precinct of Hōnen-ji temple — its Tabelog genre is literally うどん・ラーメン・つけ麺, the same three words the light record carried — but it is in Busshōzan, Takamatsu, Kagawa, not Ningyōchō
neighborhood: COULD NOT VERIFY any Tokyo location. Tabelog files 竜雲 under kagawa/A3701/A370101 (仏生山駅), about 20 minutes by car from Takamatsu station.
hours_raw: 11:00 - 15:00（L.O. 14:30）／定休日：火曜日・金曜日 — these are the Kagawa shop's hours.
gf_detail: Wheat udon is the entire menu, and the house dipping sauces are sesame-and-white-miso or curry over wheat noodles. No gluten-free claim exists. Not assessed further, because the record's location is wrong — see the note below before using anything here.
vegan_detail: Nothing published either way. The signature orders reviewers name are ごまだれ牛肉つけうどん (beef) and 和風中華そば, and Sanuki tsuyu is normally iriko/bonito dashi, so an accidental vegan meal should not be assumed. Not assessed further — the record is mislocated.

chef_bio.origin: Busshōzan, Takamatsu, Kagawa — inside the grounds of Hōnen-ji, the Matsudaira family temple of the Takamatsu domain
chef_bio.background: 竜雲 opened in December 1991 and seats 40. What makes it locally famous is where it stands: on the temple approach inside Hōnen-ji's precinct, so reviewers describe eating the 竜雲盛り zaru udon and then climbing the temple steps for the view of the five-storey pagoda and the ponds. The house style is a sesame-dare tsuke-udon eaten with a bowl of plain rice on the side. None of this belongs to Tokyo, so it has not been written up as a Tokyo bio.
chef_bio.specialty: 竜雲盛り zaru udon; ごまだれ tsuke-udon (sesame and white miso); curry udon; 和風中華そば.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog's page for 竜雲 gives 香川県高松市仏生山町甲3207-2 法然寺境内, tel 087-889-1217, 40 seats, an opening date of 1991年12月, hours 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and closures on Tuesday and Friday, and the genre string うどん、ラーメン、つけ麺. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 竜雲 returns 68 hits, of which this Kagawa shop is the only exact-name restaurant; the nearest Tokyo entries are 龍雲庵 (a kaiseki restaurant at Shin-Ochanomizu, a different name and a different cuisine) and two supermarket entries in Nozawa. No source places a restaurant called 竜雲 in Ningyōchō or anywhere in Chūō-ku.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not send anyone in Ningyōchō here. The only restaurant called 竜雲 on Tabelog is a temple-precinct udon shop in Takamatsu, Kagawa, roughly 600 km from Nihonbashi. The Tokyo pin has been left at its original approximate coordinates and loc_precise is false; the record should be deleted from the Tokyo dataset.

name: 山本山 ふじヱ茶房
address_ja: 〒103-6101 東京都中央区日本橋2-5-1 日本橋髙島屋三井ビルディング 1階
cuisine: The tearoom of the 1690 tea-and-nori house Yamamotoyama, on the street where it was founded — gyokuro and sencha brewed cup by cup at the counter (¥1,300–¥2,300 a serving) alongside nori-centred meals: 膳 にほんばし ¥2,800, 膳 海苔鯛茶漬け ¥2,400, 海苔めん ¥1,800, 玉露茶蕎麦 ¥2,300, and the ¥2,200 にほんばし海苔弁当 to take away
neighborhood: Nihonbashi 2-chōme, street-level in the Nihonbashi Takashimaya Mitsui Building — 1 min (124 m) from Nihonbashi station (Ginza and Tōzai lines, Toei Asakusa line), 5 min from Tokyo station's Yaesu side
hours_raw: 物販 10:30～18:00／喫茶 11:00～17:30（L.O.17:00）／お持ち帰り弁当 受付 11:00～17:00・お受取り 18:00まで／手巻き ご提供：火～土 13時～16時半(L.O.16時)／夜ふじヱ ご提供：火～土 18時～21時30分（L.O.21時）・ご予約は2日前より／定休日：不定休（年末年始）
gf_detail: Not workable. Three of the four savoury lines are wheat noodles — 玉露茶蕎麦 ¥2,300 and 玉露花巻蕎麦 ¥2,300 (green-tea soba, which in Japan is a wheat-cut noodle) and 海苔めん ¥1,800 — and the rest are 茶漬け and 海苔重, i.e. rice under ordinary wheat shōyu and a dashi pour, with 赤だし (miso) served alongside the onigiri. Nori itself is naturally gluten-free but the seasoned のりせんべい and the shop's own tsukudani-style seasonings are not declared. No gluten-free claim appears anywhere on the site or on Tabelog, and no tamari is named.
vegan_detail: Nothing is published either way, and the meal menu leans animal: 膳 海苔鯛茶漬け is sea bream, 海苔重 comes as 牛すき or 鮭, the お結び set is 梅・鮭 with 赤だし, and any 茶漬け pour will normally be a bonito dashi. Tea is the safe part — the gyokuro, sencha, matcha and hōjicha list is long and plant-based — and 抹茶わらびもち ¥1,200, 抹茶白玉ぜんざい ¥1,000 and 玉露抹茶羊羹 ¥650 are plausible, but the shop does not state their ingredients and 玉露嶺岡とうふ ¥1,600 is a mineoka-dōfu, a preparation traditionally set with milk. Ask before ordering anything but the tea.

roles: operated by 山本山株式会社 (Yamamotoyama Co., Ltd.), founded 1690
chef_bio.origin: Nihonbashi, Chūō-ku — the street where Yamamotoyama has traded since 元禄三年 (1690)
chef_bio.background: Yamamotoyama's own copy tells the story plainly: the house was founded in 1690 as one of Nihonbashi's tea merchants, and the Meiji-era 茶業通鑑 records that when Nagatani Sōen invented sencha it was 山本嘉兵衛商店 — the firm that became Yamamotoyama — that first sold it. ふじヱ茶房 is the company's return to that founding site, opened as 「次の300年に向かうために、新しい文化を発信する場として」 — a place to carry the culture into the next three hundred years. It is a small room, 25 seats (6 at the counter, 19 at tables), where staff cool the water and brew each serving to order; the first Yamamoto Kahei's line 「おいしいお茶を、こんなにおいしいのだから、多くの人に味わっていただきたい」 is printed at the top of the site. The company's store page lists it as one of six group venues, the others being the kappō-kaiseki 山本山 嘉兵衛, an ochazuke-and-onigiri counter, a wa-café, PEAK S PEAK CAFE and the YMY GYOKURO TEAROOM. No individual chef is named publicly.
chef_bio.philosophy: 不易流行 — hold the tradition and keep changing. Tea served as an act of hospitality rather than a drink: 「ひと手間を惜しまず、お客様のために尽くすこと。それが江戸の商家としての私たちのおもてなしの心です。」
chef_bio.specialty: 玉露しふく ¥3,300, a course that walks the same gyokuro through changing brew temperatures with a wagashi; 膳 にほんばし ¥2,800; にほんばし海苔弁当 ¥2,200, sold for consumption within four hours; the 茶菓講 afternoon tea at ¥6,000 (sencha) / ¥8,000 (gyokuro).

anecdotes.text: The shop warns that its door is not inside the Takashimaya S.C. — 「※入口は髙島屋S.C内にはございません。路面からのアクセスとなります。」 — you reach it from the street.
There is a tea-and-spirits list nobody expects from a 336-year-old tea house: matcha with vodka, sencha with gin, hōjicha with rum, genmaicha with whisky, all ¥1,300–¥1,500, plus a matcha beer.
A Tabelog regular records buying the ¥2,200 海苔弁当 for the fourth time and notes the price has not moved since his first visit two years earlier.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: fujie.yamamotoyama.co.jp gives the address 〒103-6101 東京都中央区日本橋2-5-1 日本橋髙島屋三井ビルディング1階, the phone 03-3271-3273, the split 物販/喫茶/弁当 hours, the street-entrance warning, the full priced menu and the 1690 founding history. Tabelog 13226924 confirms the same address and phone, 25 seats, 11:00–17:30 (L.O. 17:00) daily with 不定休（年末年始）, a ¥3,000–¥3,999 band and a 3.21 rating over 225 reviews. yamamotoyama.co.jp/store/ lists ふじヱ茶房 and 嘉兵衛 as the group's Nihonbashi venues.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 25-seat kitchen that boils wheat noodles (茶蕎麦, 花巻蕎麦, 海苔めん) to order in the same small space as everything else. No wheat-free handling is claimed anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat shōyu should be assumed throughout — the 茶漬け, 海苔重 and noodle tsuyu all rest on it, and no tamari or gluten-free seasoning is mentioned on the site or on Tabelog.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The savoury menu is fish- and beef-led (鯛茶漬け, 海苔重 牛すき, 海苔重 鮭, お結び 鮭) with 赤だし alongside; dashi content of the 茶漬け pour is not published.

positives.text: Reservations are taken by a human on 03-3271-3273 — the shop states it does not use auto-reserve — so a dietary question can actually be asked and answered before you arrive.

cultural_comfort.note: One minute from Nihonbashi station, but look for the street-level door: the shop states its entrance is not inside the Takashimaya S.C. The site has an English version at fujie.yamamotoyama.co.jp/e/, and in-store and takeaway bookings both run through TableCheck, so you do not need to telephone in Japanese unless you want to ask about ingredients — for that, 03-3271-3273 is answered by staff, and the shop notes the line is often busy. Twenty-five seats and a well-known ¥2,200 nori bentō mean midday queues; the 弁当 is sold for eating within four hours, so it is a lunch to take to a bench, not a souvenir to carry home.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「山本山 本店」, 海苔・伝統料理, 日本橋駅周辺. There is no venue trading under that exact name today: Tabelog's two 山本山 日本橋本店 entries are flagged 【移転】 (13011466, old address 日本橋2-5-2) and 【閉店】 (13206787). The Yamamotoyama venue operating on the founding site now is 山本山 ふじヱ茶房 at 日本橋2-5-1, confirmed by the company's own store index and by the shop's own site, and its nori-and-tea menu matches the light record's 海苔・伝統料理 tag. Confidence is 'medium' because that identification is an inference, though a well-supported one; note also that a different, unrelated company — 山本海苔店 — runs its own 日本橋本店 a few hundred metres away at Mitsukoshimae, which is an easy confusion to make with this name. Coordinates are ふじヱ茶房's own, about 900 m from the original approximate pin.

name: 中国料理 龍門 浜町本店
address_ja: 〒103-0007 東京都中央区日本橋浜町2-37-10 浜商事ビル
cuisine: A big, cheap, genuinely Chinese-run machi-chūka over two floors — 100-plus dishes from ¥300, lunch from ¥950, a three-dishes-from-68 set at ¥1,780, and house Peking duck at ¥4,200 for a half bird; the plate regulars come back for is the 黒酢の酢豚, black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork, ¥1,080
neighborhood: Nihonbashi-Hamachō 2-chōme, ten seconds from Hamachō station exit A1 (Toei Shinjuku line) behind the Meijiza theatre — about 600 m east of Ningyōchō station (Hibiya and Toei Asakusa lines), which HotPepper also lists among its nearest stations
gf_detail: Not workable. The published menu is wheat end to end: eight noodle dishes (ラーメン ¥850, タン麺, 坦々麺, ワンタンメン, 海鮮五目焼きそば), a whole 揚げ物 section of battered and floured frying (鶏の唐揚げ, 揚げワンタン, 油淋鶏, 黒酢の酢豚), wrappers through the entire 点心 list (餃子, 小籠包, ニラ饅頭, 春巻き), and Peking duck served with wheat pancakes. The seasoning base is ordinary wheat 醤油 with oyster sauce and starch-thickened gravies; no gluten-free claim, no tamari, and no allergen information is published on HotPepper or Tabelog. The one non-wheat noodle, 焼きビーフン ¥1,050, is rice vermicelli but is wok-fried in shared pans and sauced with soy.
vegan_detail: Nothing is published either way and nothing on the menu is labelled vegetarian. The plausible candidates are all cold 前菜 — 冷やしトマト ¥600, 冷製胡瓜 ¥650, ジャガイモ千切りの塩和え ¥680, ザーサイ ¥600 — plus ほうれん草炒め ¥700 among the hot vegetables. But 中華風豆腐 and ピータン豆腐 carry preserved egg, 麻婆豆腐 / 麻婆茄子 / 麻婆春雨 are normally built on minced pork, and a machi-chūka kitchen this size usually seasons its vegetable stir-fries with chicken stock or lard. Treat each of these as a question to ask, not an option to assume.

roles: Chinese-run family operation; no chef named publicly
chef_bio.origin: Nihonbashi-Hamachō, Chūō-ku — behind the Meijiza theatre
chef_bio.background: 龍門 is the older of two sibling shops: a reviewer who eats at the Kodenmachō branch monthly writes that he only discovered the Hamachō shop behind the Meijiza, and that staff told him Hamachō opened first. It is a 95-seat room over two floors, white-walled and plain rather than smart, with cooks the reviewers hear speaking Cantonese and Mandarin and a Japanese-speaking floor manager. Ordering is by tablet; payment takes cards, transport IC and the full run of QR wallets including Alipay and WeChat Pay. The shop's own promotional copy leans on banquet trade — private hire, 宴会 courses from ¥3,500 with two hours of free drinks, and an offer to cook Chinese dishes that are not on the menu if you ask in advance — which is what a 95-seat room between a theatre and an office district lives on. HotPepper reviewers score it 4.8 over 68 reviews, mostly 友人・知人と (56%) and 会社の宴会 (22%); Tabelog's harder-marking crowd gives 3.30 over 62.
chef_bio.specialty: 黒酢の酢豚 ¥1,080, the dish reviewers name first; 自家製北京ダック, ¥4,200 a half bird or ¥8,000 whole; the ¥1,780 three-dish set chosen from 68 items; ¥950 lunches.

anecdotes.text: A regular of the Kodenmachō branch found the Hamachō shop by accident behind the Meijiza and was told by staff that Hamachō was the original — 「スタッフに伺うと、浜町店が先にオープンしたそうです」.
Another reviewer describes walking past for months while shopping at the greengrocer opposite before working up the nerve to eat alone: 「勇気を出してお一人様で入店して来ました。店構えはお洒落では無く普通の町中華」.
The shop advertises that it will cook off-menu Chinese dishes on advance request — 「メニューに載っていない中国料理もお作り致します」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13101467 gives the name 龍門, the address 東京都中央区日本橋浜町2-37-10, coordinates 35.68883/139.78715, tel 03-6661-9276, 95 seats, genre 中華料理・四川料理, a ¥3,000–¥3,999 band, hours 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–23:00 with Sunday closed, and a 3.30 rating over 62 reviews. HotPepper strJ000816251 lists the same shop as 中国料理 龍門 浜町本店 at 日本橋浜町2-37-10 浜商事ビル, one minute from Hamachō exit A1, with the full priced food menu last updated 2026-05-04 and a 4.8 rating over 68 reviews. Tabelog 13191364 is the sibling 中国料理龍門 小伝馬町店 at 日本橋大伝馬町1-3 アスカVビル B1F, seven minutes on foot from Ningyōchō exit A5.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 95-seat machi-chūka with a dedicated deep-fry section and eight wheat-noodle dishes. Flour, wrappers and noodles are in constant use across shared woks and one fryer; no wheat-free handling is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat 醤油 should be assumed throughout, alongside oyster sauce and starch-thickened gravies. No tamari or gluten-free seasoning appears on the menu or in either directory listing.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The vegetable section sits on the same line as pork, beef and seafood: 麻婆 dishes are normally pork-based, ピータン豆腐 and カニ玉 carry egg, and stir-fry stock is not declared.

positives.text: Ordering is by tablet, which lets you read every dish name at your own pace instead of negotiating at speed — useful if you are checking ingredients word by word.

cultural_comfort.level: Easy, but bring your own Japanese for ingredients
cultural_comfort.note: One of the easiest rooms in the area to walk into alone — 95 seats over two floors, tablet ordering, no reservation needed at lunch, and every payment method including Alipay and WeChat Pay. Reviewers specifically note that solo diners are normal here. Floor staff answer in polite Japanese but the kitchen is Cantonese- and Mandarin-speaking, so an allergy conversation is better written down than spoken; there is no English menu and no published allergen chart. Evenings tilt towards company parties and the room is loud. Note the branch ambiguity flagged in the enrich note: if you head for Ningyōchō rather than Hamachō, the sibling 中国料理龍門 小伝馬町店 (日本橋大伝馬町1-3, 7 min from exit A5) is the one you reach first.

enrich_note: Confirmed as a real Tokyo business, but the light record's description was wrong and the branch is ambiguous. The record read 「龍門」, 'Ramen / Tsukemen - celebrated local favorite', 人形町. 龍門 is not a ramen shop: it is a 95-seat Chinese restaurant, filed by Tabelog under 中華料理・四川料理, whose menu carries ramen at ¥850 as one line among a hundred. The cuisine string has been rewritten accordingly. neighborhood: Uchi-Kanda 2-chōme, 245 m and two minutes from Kanda station's west exit (JR Yamanote, Chūō, Keihin-Tōhoku and Tokyo Metro Ginza lines) — a block from the queue at わいず, in what reviewers call Kanda's ramen war zone

gf_detail: Not workable, and not close. The entire product is a bowl of thick wheat noodles — Tabelog's own tags for the shop are つけ麺・太麺・ストレート麺 — and the dipping broth starts from a kaeshi the owner states is built on Akita-prefecture soy sauce, i.e. ordinary wheat shōyu. There is no gluten-free claim anywhere on the shop's site, its Instagram, or Tabelog, no tamari, and no published allergen information. With seven seats and one noodle boiler there is no separable line.
vegan_detail: Not possible. The house soup is explicitly an animal-and-fish stock: the shop describes pressure-cooking the base and then layering three kinds of kombu, three kinds of fish and shiitake over it, and the standard bowl is served with chāshū. There is no vegetable or plant-based option on a menu that consists of one dish in two or three sizes.

roles: 店主 (owner-chef, based at the Shinbashi honten; makes the soup for every branch)
chef_bio.origin: Shinbashi, Minato-ku — 麺屋周郷's original five-seat counter at 新橋4-19-1
chef_bio.background: 麺屋周郷 began as a five-seat tsukemen counter in Shinbashi under the motto 「完成なき一杯を目指して」 — aiming for a bowl that is never finished. The owner still makes the soup for every branch himself at the honten and sends it out, which is unusual enough that the shop says so on its front page. The Kanda shop opened on 1 September 2023 as 神田周郷 and does not reproduce the Shinbashi bowl: it takes the same soup and turns it into 赤つけ麺, adding a chilli oil made from spices ground on a stone mill each morning and then layering several more spices on top of that. It is seven counter seats, no reservations, cash only, and it shuts on Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays — three days a week — with a standing notice that it also closes at short notice 「より良い味をご提供するため」. Reviewers describe an 11:00 opening with six people already waiting, the bowls finished in one lot, and a shop that has recently re-plated onto better vessels; several note the owner himself is often behind the counter here rather than at Shinbashi. Tabelog has it at 3.69 across 799 reviews. The group also sells the two bowls frozen by mail order at ¥1,600 each.
chef_bio.philosophy: 完成なき一杯を目指して — aiming for a bowl that is never finished; keep evolving in order to make it better.
chef_bio.specialty: 赤つけ麺特製 — the Kanda-only chilli tsukemen, with the stone-milled rāyu; 辛つけ麺 at about ¥1,300; reviewers say the bowl is designed to be completed by ordering the 〆 rice at the end.

anecdotes.text: The Kanda bowl is not the Shinbashi bowl: the shop's own copy says the master's soup is finished here with 「毎朝職人が石臼で挽いたスパイスで作る香り高い辣油」 — a chilli oil from spices ground on a stone mill each morning.

A March 2026 reviewer arrived at 10:57 and was sixth in line; the bowl came at 11:10 because the shop finishes a whole lot at once. He noted the vessels had been upgraded and that the owner was working the counter.
An August 2026 reviewer walked over from Nihonbashi, found a twenty-deep queue at the neighbouring famous shop わいず, moved on — and found 周郷 full too.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop states its kaeshi is built on Akita-prefecture soy sauce — ordinary wheat shōyu. No tamari or gluten-free seasoning is mentioned.

cultural_comfort.note: Two minutes from Kanda west exit, no reservations, cash only — bring notes. Seven counter seats and a shop that cooks in lots means arriving before 11:00 or after 13:30 if you do not want to wait; reviewers routinely report six or more people ahead of them at opening. Check before you go: the Kanda branch closes three days a week (Wed, Sat, Sun), warns that it shuts early when ingredients run out, and posts unscheduled closures on its site banner and on Instagram @menya_sugo_aka. Note this shop is genuinely spicy — 赤 in 赤つけ麺 means the chilli version, and it is the only style Kanda serves; the plain bowl is at the Shinbashi honten, 東京都港区新橋4-19-1. No English menu, but the menu is effectively one dish.
